page: The UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-48GB is a cloud server configuration within the Cloud Native family. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, this x86_64 system provides 16 shared vCPUs mapped to AMD EPYC 7542 processors running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system includes 48.0 GB of RAM, yielding 3.0 GB of memory per core. Cache resources include 64 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. It contains standard instruction extensions such as AVX, AES, and SHA-NI, but lacks AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets. Local storage is not bundled, requiring external network block storage, and there are no onboard GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses included.

Benchmark results show balanced general-purpose execution with varying CPU characteristics. In Geekbench testing, the server demonstrates strong single-core performance scoring 2089.0, alongside strong ratings in image processing (14068.0) and text processing (2835.0). However, sustained stress testing displays divergence: stress-ng single-core performance falls in the bottom 10% (787.49), while multi-core stress testing reaches an average 12555.22. PassMark CPU testing registers an average score of 28502.96, and PassMark memory testing registers 2231.86. Memory bandwidth reaches 82.52 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 39.0 GB/sec for uncached write operations.

Because CPU cores are shared rather than dedicated, heavy computational tasks may experience variable contention during peak host usage. Cost efficiency is balanced toward horizontal throughput rather than sustained single-threaded compute density, making it cost-effective for distributed cloud-native microservices. The configuration suits container orchestration worker nodes, CI/CD compilation workloads, mid-sized relational database replicas, Redis caching clusters, and general web application serving.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-48GB is a KVM-based virtual server powered by 16 shared vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 7542 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, coupled with 48.0 GB of system memory (3.0 GB per core). It features an x86_64 architecture with 16 MB of L3 cache, standard vector extensions, and cryptographic acceleration, but does not provide AVX-512 instructions, local storage disks, GPUs, or bundled public IPv4 addresses. Benchmark performance is balanced across most metrics, scoring 2089.0 in Geekbench single-core and 14914.0 in multi-core tests, alongside 28502.96 in PassMark CPU. While stress-ng single-core metrics fall into the lower percentiles due to shared CPU allocation, its memory bandwidth and multi-core throughput remain solid. It is well matched for containerized microservices, build pipelines, Redis instances, and standard web serving workloads.
